title: Understanding PCA and SVD
text: PCA (Principal Component Analysis) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It is often used to make data easy to explore and visualize. SVD (Singular Value Decomposition) is a method used in PCA to decompose a matrix into three other matrices.

title: Matrix Decomposition in SVD
text: In SVD, a matrix X is decomposed into three matrices: U, S, and $$V^T$$. The matrix S contains the singular values, which are the square roots of the eigenvalues of $$X^T$$ X.

title: Role of Singular Values
text: The singular values in matrix S indicate the amount of variance captured by each principal component. Larger singular values correspond to components that capture more variance.

hintAnswer: The first component captures the most variance followed by the second and then the third.
